title: Autocode status payload
description: The one JSON object `autocode --run-dir RUN --status` prints, and the one `autocode ... --json` prints on stdout for a run that has loaded: a completed or paused run prints this payload; a user action, or any other invocation that loaded the run and returned without printing the payload itself, adds `result`. A refusal before the run loads prints only `{"result": ...}`: that object does not validate against this root, which requires the payload's fields; its `result` validates against `#/properties/result`. A setting the run's configuration refuses as the run loads (such as `--single-model` or `--spec-first` on a saved run, or a tool-containment refusal: `--allow-uncontained-tools` where it does not apply, or a built-in OpenCode run without it where the kernel tool boundary is unavailable; docs/cli.md lists more) adds `result` to the saved run's payload, or prints `{"result": ...}` alone before a new run's first checkpoint, and still ends with `autocode: ...` on stderr; the refused setting is not saved. A native visual run (a `VISUAL_REVIEW_PROFILE=` task) instead saves that refusal as a `PAUSED_INVALID_OUTPUT` pause and prints it like any other pause, with `result.error` null. Any other invocation that ends with an error message (`autocode: ...` or argparse's usage text on stderr) prints nothing on stdout. The fields a program acts on are in `view`, the status view contract (docs/task-run.md#status-view): fields are added, never renamed or removed, and `view.schema` changes if a meaning must. Every field this schema requires is always present; unlisted fields are allowed and a consumer must ignore the ones it does not know. The keywords used here (type, enum, required, properties, items) are the subset tools/autocode_util.validate_schema checks, so the CLI's own acceptance test validates the status payloads against this file. Exit codes: docs/cli.md#exit-codes.

workspace.description: The checkout the run works in: its task worktree, or the project itself for an in-place run.

project_workspace.description: The project the task worktree was created from.

task_branch.description: The task worktree's branch; null for an in-place run.

status.description: The saved status; the same as view.status.

stale.description: True when the saved status says RUNNING but the recorded stage or runner check has no live supervised result; next_action then says what must happen first.

next_action.description: What must happen before anything else when the checkpoint is stale; null otherwise.

view.description: The status view (tools/autocode_run_view.py, docs/task-run.md#status-view), with `progress` and `delivery` added by the status command.

execution.description: Core lifetime capability. Older clients ignore this additive field; clients reading older cores treat its absence as unknown.

observation.description: Read-only sample metadata supplied by the status command. sampled_at identifies this read and may differ between equivalent status requests; checkpoint_token identifies saved state and grants no action authority. Null in an uninspected pure projection.

attention.description: Versioned current human-boundary or completed-turn identity. Acknowledgement records only this local OS user's read state, never task approval or delivery verification. Missing fields in older cores mean unknown.

id.description: Opaque core identity for this run incarnation and current decision context or completed same-chat turn; grants no task authority.

summary.description: Bounded, redacted task snippet, never raw provider output.

acknowledge.description: Only this acknowledgement's exact named argument array may be dispatched; it answers no question and approves no plan.

schema.description: The view's version; it changes only if a field's meaning changes.

status.description: The exact run status, such as RUNNING, WAITING_FOR_USER, AWAITING_GOAL_APPROVAL, a PAUSED_* status or TASK_COMPLETE.

done.description: True when the task completed: status TASK_COMPLETE or COMPLETE, and not a replay with recorded checks.

needs.description: What must happen next for the run to progress; null when it is complete. `kind` is an open vocabulary (approve_plan, answer, review, resume, continue, ...); `continue` means no person input is needed, including when the core names a deterministic recovery action in `next_command`.

confirmation_required.description: False only for a plain resume of a clean requested pause: the Resume click needs no duplicate dialog. It remains person-only and never authorizes automatic continuation. Missing retains the client's confirmation policy.

pause_category.description: Whose action a stopped run needs; null for an active or completed run.

next_command.description: The command that answers `needs`, with issued tokens passed through their environment variables; placeholders such as ANSWER are left for a person. Null for an active or completed run.

workflow.description: The kind of job recognized from the request (build, bugfix, review, design, discuss); null until recognized.

turn.description: Which request of the conversation the run is on: 1, then one more per --follow-up.

evidence.description: What the run agreed to deliver and what supports it.

approvals.description: Who approved each plan and review, edited the plan, resumed the run from a pause or accepted its completion, oldest first (#722). Recorded as given and never verified.

usage.description: Tokens and cost so far; unknown cost is not zero.

execution_identity.description: Frozen launch identity, validated against the attempt. Empty object for legacy, unknown or contradictory facts. Known records have schema 1 and all identity fields; billing is a saved selected-route classification, not an invoice. Endpoints identify configured targets, not redirects or compatibility.

reasoning_effort.description: Effective launch effort; blank/null can preserve the provider default.
Effective effort when recorded; absent on historical attempts.

progress.description: How far the run has got, from saved records; `line` is for a person, the fields beside it for programs.

summary.description: The run in one sentence (#2049). `state` is `done` only when completion is verified against the current checkout; a finished run without that, or a running checkpoint nothing supervises, is `stopped`. `next_command` is the view's own `next_command` (null when done).

review_result.description: Read-time review inspection, separate from authenticated evidence.workflow_result; null until inspected. Includes recorded outcome/artifact/source binding, freshness and reasons.

escalations.description: Each escalation the run made, oldest first (#612): a role's climb on its effort ladder or the Builder's stronger attempt, with the role and stage it was for, the route it climbed from and to, its escalated attempts and what they cost, and how it ended. Empty when the run made none (docs/task-run.md#status-view).

role.description: The route role whose route moved (a settings.roles key: sol, terra, completion, resolver).

stage.description: The stage that struggled, else the first escalated attempt's; null when neither is recorded.

job.description: That stage's job as the screen names it (Tester, Builder, ...; tools/autocode_roles.py); the route role's when the stage is not known; null when neither names a job.

trigger.description: What set it off: validation_rework, rejected_output, no_progress or abandoned_attempt for a climb; execution_failure for the stronger attempt.

task_id.description: The task it was for; for the stronger attempt, the task of the failed attempt its decision names.

deferred_by_parallel_builder.description: True when a parallel Builder left this stronger attempt to the parent run, which made it serially.

inherited.description: True when it was made before this run was created, in the run a checkpoint continuation restored: its attempts there are not in this run's records, so its cost is unknown (cost.usd null, or a floor of its attempts since the restore), never zero.

basis.description: The provider's reported cost, tokens at the dated table, unpriced, or still running.

cost.description: What the escalated attempts cost at the dated price table, as the view's `cost` prices a stage. A null amount is unknown, never zero; while `complete` is false, `usd` is a floor. 0 only when no attempt launched in a run that made the escalation itself and has a launch route on every record of the role after it.

unrouted_attempts.description: The role's stage records after it, within its attempts' span, saved without a launch route (before 2026-10-01): they may be its attempts but cannot be shown to be, so they are not in `attempts`, nothing they did decides its outcome, and while there are any `complete` is false and `usd` is null when no listed attempt is priced.

progress.description: Optional core-authored activity, saved progress counts and recent attempt descriptions. A finished attempt does not mean its result passed verification.

activity.description: Optional display-only events of the running, supervised attempt, oldest first. A command that exited 0 is not a passed check; never proof, approval or authority to retry.

displayed_plan.description: Present while a sealed plan is displayed for approval. milestones and end_to_end_flow (#2434) carry the completion order the person approves and are present only where the contract body has them; sealed legacy plans omit both.

approved_contract.description: Present once a plan is approved.

workspace.description: The run's effective workspace; after bootstrap relocation it can differ from the handle a client started with.

run_dir.description: The run's effective run directory, compared with a named command's run before it is taken.

planning_depth.description: How much planning the run chose and why (docs/adaptive-planning.md); documented in docs/task-run.md.

stage_policy.description: Which planning path a bug-fix run took and why (docs/adaptive-planning.md#compact-planning-for-bug-fixes): path, reasons, basis, decisions and fallback; null when the run never decided. Documented in docs/task-run.md.

pause.description: The boundary pause a working run offers: label, effect, requested and next_command. Null when nothing is working.

package.description: The repository directory a run started with --package works in; null for a run of the whole repository.

tool_containment_backend.description: The kernel boundary the latest contained launch ran in; null until a stage launches contained.

changes_by_criterion.description: Saved Builder steps attributed to the approved plan's criteria; null until a plan is approved. Attribution, not proof.

dev_server.description: The run's development server: configured, status, url, code_checkpoint, restarts and waiting.

identity.description: Opaque identity of the current user turn and grounded external work; grants no plan approval.

source_quote.description: Verbatim ticket or requirement text grounding this repository's involvement.

evidence.description: Cited file and optional line range grounding this repository's involvement.

linked.description: The other runs of this run's change set (autocode changeset link): the source run and each linked run, with the repository it covers; run_dir is null while a linked run is starting.

briefs.description: A ready brief for each repository the request spans, this one first, for a person who stops here and runs them separately.

scope.description: Work the request places in another repository (#2066): the grounded external parts, the targets the person left out of this run (each recorded in scope_exclusions), the exact human decision (this_repository), the core-owned assignment (linked_repositories), or null while unanswered, the targets dropped for want of a verbatim quote or a cited file, and the other runs of this run's change set (linked).

coordination.description: Automatic multi-repository coordination offer; null without an eligible bug or an existing record. Clients read status_command and take only exact named next_command or cancel_command arrays.

related_profile.description: Versioned copy of inheritable role routes and limits, excluding credentials, sessions and approvals. Installation still enforces the target project approval policy.

proxied_requirements.description: The requirements the current plan proves only on a stand-in because code outside this checkout renders what the user sees (#2068): the criteria it cites (evidence) and why (proxy_reason); [] when none or no plan yet. Documented in docs/task-run.md.

result.description: What the invocation did, under --json only: after a user action or a refused setting, after any other invocation that loaded the run without printing the payload itself, and alone for a refusal before the run loads or a setting refused before a new run's first checkpoint.

saved.description: True when exit_code is 0: the action was saved, or the task completed.

message.description: The text a person would have read on stdout.

error.description: Null unless the input was refused; also printed as `{"error": ...}` on its own line of stderr: the last one, except after a refused setting, where `autocode: ...` follows.
